deck: A president's condolence, a commencement speech, a print of a wave, and a tool for keeping data where others can find it.

paragraphs: This is a development sample. It holds one of every kind of thing the magazine can carry, so the pages can be checked before real Hauls arrive.
Each object here is set in its own printed form, and each carries the rich media a Haul can hold: code, a video, a podcast, a pull quote and a picture.

route.text: A letter from 1864, still read aloud.
A tool for publishing data, with its one command.
Both are about leaving something for strangers.

why.text: Sample note. A letter of five sentences that is still read at funerals. The form matters: a dateline, a salutation, the body, the close.

excerpt.text:
Dear Madam,
I have been shown in the files of the War Department a statement of the Adjutant General of Massachusetts that you are the mother of five sons who have died gloriously on the field of battle.

why.text: Sample note. A post set as a clipping, with the handle and the date, never the platform's embed.

excerpt.text: Keep a commonplace book. Not for anyone else. Copy out the lines that stop you. In ten years it will be the best book you own.
excerpt.highlight: Copy out the lines that stop you.

why.text: Sample note. One command turns a SQLite file into a website and an API. I use it to keep the magazine's own data browsable.

excerpt.text: An open source multi-tool for exploring and publishing data

blocks.caption: Install it and serve a database
blocks.code:
pip install datasette
datasette serve hauls.db --open
